summary: Enhance your skills with our Shadow Report Writing Training. Learn to craft impactful reports that drive change and influence decision-makers effectively.
lede: Shadow report writing turns human rights monitoring into structured, evidence-based submissions for international review. Designed for experienced practitioners in research, law, and advocacy, the training covers evidence verification, analysis of treaty obligations, and thematic prioritization. Participants also practice drafting concise recommendations and developing individual or joint submissions.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for experienced practitioners who operate at the intersection of research, law, and international advocacy.
modules: Legal Gap Analysis and State Report Review
Data Visualization and Digital Reporting Tools
Engagement with Treaty Bodies and Advocacy
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in human rights monitoring, legal research, or policy advocacy. Familiarity with the basic UN Charter and Treaty Body system is required. Note: This is a technical drafting course, not an introductory human rights course.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
